To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for correlated channels, the mutual information is a Gaussian random variable, (ii) for correlated channels with interferers, the mutual information distribution is not Gaussian, (iii) for correlated channels and with interferers, it is not possible to optimize over all possible input signal covariances, and (iv) the closed-loop capacity of multi-antennas is not a Gaussian random variable and the capacity distribution is not a Gaussian.
The use of large multi-antenna (or multi-user) arrays can provide substantial throughput gains in realistic wireless systems.
